newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher despite racketeer reports.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher despite racketeer reports.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index ended higher on Tuesday even though participants focused on reports of another major Japanese firm's suspected links with "sokaiya" racketeers.
But the Japanese media reports of a police investigation into food and seasonings maker Ajinomoto Co, coming soon after a case involving Nomura Securities, had only a limited impact on the market.
The Nikkei 225 average closed up 153.83 points or 0.85 percent at 18,267.72. Its March futures gained 130 points to 18,210 and its June futures rose by a similar amount to 18,180.
"There are no reasons to sell off now, but if more similar news comes out, it would hurt the market," said Hiroyuki Nakai, chief investment strategist at Nikko Securities.
